Route exam

Competition day checklist

  • No coaching during a competition: agree on the plan before the start
  • Read the programme first: dates, targets, schedule, fee, categories, contacts.
  • Keeping to the schedule is your own responsibility.
  • Check your score when leaving each stand; the referee decides.
  • Read the menu before you step up: trap order, special targets, type of each double.
  • Sporting™: before the call, both feet in the stand, the heel of the stock (its top back corner) on your body and below the vest line.
  • Sporting™: the vest line is 25 cm below the shoulder axis (a line through both shoulders), in a contrasting colour.
  • Sporting™: at most 15 seconds between singles or between doubles. Compak® Sporting: at most 10 seconds to call, counted from the shot at the previous station's target.
  • Be on time: in Sporting™ targets missed through lateness are zero; in Compak® Sporting by squad, coming after the squad's first call costs 25 zeros.
  • Guns stay open during the presentation; in Sporting™, firing or mock shooting at that time is penalised.
  • Only the referee decides; nobody picks up a target to check it; object at once.
  • After a failure, stay put with the gun closed and pointing down the range; opening it before the referee's check costs the target.
  • Compak® Sporting: one cartridge per target; deliberately firing both at one target is zero-zero.
  • Disagree? Protest at once on the stand, hand up, before the next call.
  • Long shorts only (no more than 5 cm above the knee); tops with sleeves (short is fine); no sandals.
  • The competitor number goes on the back, fully visible.
  • Without hearing protection or glasses, a shooter is treated as absent, in both disciplines.
  • A routine is the same steps in the same order before each target.
  • Disturbed before the call? Lower the gun, breathe out and start again.
  • Set 2–3 process goals and one realistic personal standard.
  • Check the score on the card, not during the stand.
  • Reset in 5–10 seconds: gun safe, breath out, one correction, one picture, next routine.
  • After a referee decision: protest at once and correctly, then let it go.
  • The night before: usual bedtime, kit packed, plan written down.
  • Coffee: your usual amount, and not late in the day.
  • Carry water and drink small sips through the day.
  • Familiar breakfast, small snacks; wash your hands before eating.
  • No alcohol before or during shooting.
  • Beta-blockers are prohibited in shooting at all times; treat them as prohibited in clay shooting too.
  • Check each medicine in Global DRO by its active ingredient, or ask your national anti-doping agency; check again each year.
  • Registration, competitor number on the back, squad lists and times.
  • Without hearing protection and safety glasses on the stand you are treated as absent.
  • Be ready at your turn, with cartridges for the whole round; test the gun only at the test stand.
  • Lateness costs zeros; in Compak® Sporting 25 zeros for the round.
  • Disagree? Raise your hand at once and say “protest” or “appeal”
  • Be on time (in Compak® Sporting, report to the referee before the round): if you are late, missed targets can count as zeros
  • Customs: greet, “well shot”, thank the trapper and referee
  • Call short and clear, the same way each time: “Pull!” or “Ready!”
  • Disagree at once: raise a hand and say “Protest!” (Compak® Sporting: before the next shooter calls)
  • Sporting™: check your score when leaving each stand; Compak® Sporting: sign the sheet or lose the right to complain
  • Protest immediately, on the stand, hand raised: “Protest!” / “Appeal!”
  • Protest before your next call: calling accepts the ruling (Compak® Sporting: before the next shooter calls)
  • Resume within 15 s (Sporting™) or 10 s (Compak® Sporting); further arguing = an attempt to influence the referee
  • Might you be in a shoot-off? Stay close and be ready within 15 minutes of the call.
